fr.elements: Main Residence; Solar Panel System; Walkway; Vehicle Parking Area; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Mark the detached structure with a secondary address or unit identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence.
• Keep a clear footpath between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without pushing through vegetation.
• Trim vegetation along the walkway so responders can move quickly on foot without obstruction.
• Pull back dense plantings from around both structures so responders can reach exterior walls and windows.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored items so arriving units have a consistent staging area.
• Post the solar panel system shutoff location and type on or near the main electrical panel so responders can locate it without searching.
• Mark the solar panel shutoff with a weatherproof label visible from ground level.
• Establish a turnaround area near the end of the driveway large enough for a fire or emergency vehicle to reverse direction; mark its boundaries if needed.
• Keep the single access point free of parked vehicles, equipment, and overgrown vegetation at all times so units entering and exiting do not conflict with each other.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from large trees that overhang or touch the roof and exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants growing directly against the base of the structure.
• Keep the ground beneath large trees clear of dead leaves, branches, and other fallen plant material.
• Trim the lower branches of scattered trees up from the ground to reduce how easily fire can climb into the tree canopy.
• Maintain the open terrain areas between vegetation and the structure by keeping them free of debris and dead plant material.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass without obstruction.
